newsitem.title: NORWAY: Baltic states not ready for NATO membership-Perry.
newsitem.headline: Baltic states not ready for NATO membership-Perry.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry said on Friday that the Baltic states of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania were not ready for membership in NATO, but suggested they could one day be part of the Western alliance.

"I think they are not yet ready for membership, but the emphasis is on "not yet'," he told reporters in response to questions on the planned first round of NATO enlargement next year despite opposition by Russia.
Perry spoke after a two-day meeting of NATO defence ministers in Bergen on Wednesday and Thursday to discuss Bosnia, NATO enlargement and relations with Russia.

The ministers stressed that the alliance would go ahead with plans for enlargement, and Perry on Friday praised the three democratic Baltic states, which were absorbed by the former Soviet Union in 1944.
He said they were working hard to improve their military forces and were cooperating with NATO in Bosnia and in the "Parternership for Peace" programme.
Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary are among former Soviet bloc states prominently mentioned for possible membership in NATO in a first-round decision expected by the alliance next year.

"A key feature of the military alliance is the ability to come to the defence of all other members of the alliance if they come under attack," Perry said on Friday. "Therefore each nation in the alliance has to have military forces that have some minimum capability and some degree of compatability with NATO forces."
"In my judgment the Baltic nations do not have that kind of capability yet, but they are working very hard to get it," he added.

Robert Hunter, the U.S. Ambassador to NATO, told reporters in a joint press conference with Perry: "We first want to make sure that they can be part of later enlargement, but secondly we are going to broaden, deepen, strengthen Partnership for Peace and other things so that there will be no sense of being pushed away."
